To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of computer-assisted diagnosis in breast MRI can improve the accuracy of breast cancer detection, especially for the diagnosis of small breast cancer.

1) a significant number of mammography occult lesions are detected by MRI, 2) MRI is more sensitive than mammography in detecting breast cancer, and 3) MRI is more likely than mammography to identify multifocal and multicentric disease, and is more likely to identify disease in women with dense breast tissue.

the use of computerized assessment in breast MR imaging can help radiologists to improve the diagnostic performance in the detection of breast lesions and to reduce the number of false-positive findings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system for breast cancer detection on mammograms.
the development of an intelligent system for breast cancer detection and diagnosis.
the development and validation of a new approach for computerized assessment of breast lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of breast magnetic resonance imaging in women at high risk for breast cancer has been shown to be a useful adjunct to mammography.

the results of our study suggest that the use of a computer-aided detection (CAD) device for the detection of breast cancer on mammograms may have a small effect on cancer detection rates, and that the results of the study are inconclusive regarding the effect of the CAD device on recall rates.
the use of a computerized assessment of mammographic density is not a useful adjunct to clinical assessment in the detection of breast cancer, and that it should not be used in clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a new method for detecting clinically and mammographically occult lesions on MR images of the breast.
the use of computer-aided detection (CAD) systems for breast cancer screening is a promising technique that is likely to improve the accuracy of breast cancer screening.
the use of a computer-assisted system in conjunction with the clinical reading of MR images of the breast may improve the sensitivity of the clinical reading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that a deep learning model can detect breast lesions on MRI with high accuracy.
the combination of MRI with a computerized assessment tool can improve the detection of clinically and mammographically occult lesions.
the current clinical practice of using the breast density to guide screening mammography recommendations should be re-evaluated.
